testName: IISER IAT - The d- & f-block elements (20 Questions)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: What is the correct ground-state electronic configuration of Gadolinium (Atomic number = 64)?
questions.explanation: Gadolinium (Z=64) exhibits an anomaly. After filling the 6s orbital (Z=56), the remaining 8 electrons do not all go into 4f. To achieve the extra stability of a half-filled 4f subshell, it takes a 4f^7 configuration, and the last electron enters the 5d orbital: [Xe] 4f^7 5d^1 6s^2.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Among the entire d-block elements, which of the following elements exhibits the highest oxidation state in its typical compounds?
options: Chromium (Cr)
Manganese (Mn)
Osmium (Os)
Platinum (Pt)
questions.explanation: The highest oxidation state in the d-block is +8, exhibited by Osmium in OsO4 and Ruthenium in RuO4.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Based on the melting point trends graph (which shows peaks at Cr, Mo, W and dips at Mn, Tc), what is the primary quantum-mechanical reason for the anomalously lower melting point of Manganese compared to Chromium?
options: Manganese has a larger atomic radius, weakening the internuclear attraction.
Manganese has a stable half-filled 3d^5 configuration, holding its d-electrons tightly and preventing them from participating effectively in metallic bonding.
Manganese has fewer unpaired electrons than Chromium.
Manganese forms a covalent network lattice rather than a metallic lattice.
questions.explanation: Manganese has a perfectly half-filled 3d^5 configuration. These electrons are highly stable and tightly held by the nucleus, reducing their ability to delocalize into the metallic 'sea of electrons', which sharply weakens the metallic bonds and lowers the melting point.
questions.imagePrompt: A 2D line graph plotting Melting Point (y-axis) against Atomic Number (x-axis) for the 3d, 4d, and 5d transition series. The curves show sharp maxima exactly at Group 6 elements (Cr, Mo, W) and anomalous sharp dips at Group 7 elements (Mn, Tc).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Due to lanthanoid contraction, certain pairs of elements belonging to the 4d and 5d transition series possess almost identical atomic and ionic radii. Which of the following is one such 'chemical twin' pair?
options: Scandium (Sc) and Yttrium (Y)
Zirconium (Zr) and Hafnium (Hf)
Chromium (Cr) and Tungsten (W)
Iron (Fe) and Osmium (Os)
questions.explanation: Lanthanoid contraction causes the 5d elements to shrink in size to match the 4d elements above them. Zirconium (160 pm) and Hafnium (159 pm) are the most famous example of chemical twins.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Calculate the spin-only magnetic moment (μ) for the divalent aqueous ion of an element with atomic number 26.
questions.explanation: Z=26 is Iron. Fe ground state: [Ar] 3d^6 4s^2. Fe^2+ ion: [Ar] 3d^6. A d^6 configuration has 4 unpaired electrons (n=4). Spin-only moment = √(n(n+2)) = √(4*6) = √24 ≈ 4.90 BM.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Let M be the molar mass of KMnO4. What is the equivalent weight of KMnO4 in strongly acidic, faintly alkaline/neutral, and strongly alkaline mediums, respectively?
questions.explanation: Acidic: +7 to +2 (change=5) -> M/5. Neutral/Faintly Basic: +7 to +4 (change=3) -> M/3. Strongly Alkaline: +7 to +6 (change=1) -> M/1.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following equations correctly represents the effect of adding an alkali to a dichromate solution?
options: Cr2O7(2-) + 2OH- -> 2CrO4(2-) + H2O (Orange to Yellow)
Cr2O7(2-) + 2OH- -> 2CrO4(2-) + H2O (Yellow to Orange)
2CrO4(2-) + 2H+ -> Cr2O7(2-) + H2O (Orange to Yellow)
Cr2O7(2-) + 2H+ -> 2CrO4(2-) + H2O (Yellow to Orange)
questions.explanation: Dichromate (orange) converts to chromate (yellow) upon the addition of a base (alkali, OH-). The balanced reaction is Cr2O7(2-) + 2OH- -> 2CrO4(2-) + H2O.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Match the following processes with their correct catalyst: (i) Haber's Process, (ii) Contact Process, (iii) Wacker Process, (iv) Ziegler-Natta Polymerization.
options: (i)-Iron, (ii)-V2O5, (iii)-PdCl2, (iv)-TiCl4 mix
(i)-V2O5, (ii)-Iron, (iii)-PdCl2, (iv)-TiCl4 mix
(i)-Iron, (ii)-V2O5, (iii)-TiCl4 mix, (iv)-PdCl2
(i)-PdCl2, (ii)-V2O5, (iii)-Iron, (iv)-TiCl4 mix
questions.explanation: Haber = Iron; Contact = V2O5; Wacker = PdCl2; Ziegler-Natta = TiCl4 + Al(C2H5)3.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following statements completely and correctly explains the redox behavior of Ce^4+ and Eu^2+ in aqueous solutions?
options: Ce^4+ is a strong reducing agent because it achieves an empty 4f^0 shell, while Eu^2+ is a strong oxidizing agent due to its 4f^7 half-filled stability.
Ce^4+ is a strong oxidizing agent because it naturally reverts to the most stable +3 state of lanthanoids, whereas Eu^2+ acts as a strong reducing agent to achieve the stable +3 state.
Both Ce^4+ and Eu^2+ are highly stable and do not undergo redox reactions in aqueous media.
Eu^2+ oxidizes water to liberate oxygen gas, while Ce^4+ reduces water to liberate hydrogen gas.
questions.explanation: The +3 state is universally the most stable for lanthanoids. Ce^4+ will gain an electron to become Ce^3+ (acting as an oxidizing agent). Eu^2+ will lose an electron to become Eu^3+ (acting as a reducing agent).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Based on standard electrode potentials, why is Copper the only element in the 3d series with a positive E°(M^2+/M) value (+0.34 V)?
options: Its extremely high hydration enthalpy overcomes the ionization enthalpies.
The sum of its sublimation enthalpy and its 1st & 2nd ionization enthalpies is so high that it is not compensated by the hydration enthalpy of Cu^2+.
Copper forms a passive oxide layer, artificially inflating its electrode potential.
The filled 3d^10 configuration in solid copper makes it thermodynamically unstable.
questions.explanation: For Cu, the high energy required to atomize it and remove two electrons (sublimation + IE1 + IE2) is not fully balanced by the negative hydration enthalpy of Cu^2+. This results in a positive standard electrode potential.
questions.imagePrompt: A line graph displaying the Standard Electrode Potential (E°) for the M^2+ / M couple across the 3d transition series from Titanium (Ti) to Zinc (Zn). Most values are negative, but the curve crosses the zero-axis into positive territory exactly at Copper (Cu).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following is an INCORRECT characteristic of interstitial compounds formed by transition metals?
options: They have remarkably high melting points, higher than those of pure metals.
They retain metallic conductivity.
They are chemically extremely reactive due to the trapped non-metal atoms.
They are very hard, with some borides approaching the hardness of diamond.
questions.explanation: Interstitial compounds are chemically highly inert, not highly reactive. The inclusion of small non-metals stabilizes the metallic lattice.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: According to the balanced chemical equation for the disproportionation of the manganate ion in an acidic medium, how many moles of the purple permanganate ion are produced from 3 moles of the manganate ion?
options: 1 mole
2 moles
3 moles
4 moles
questions.explanation: Balanced equation: 3MnO4(2-) + 4H+ -> 2MnO4- + MnO2 + 2H2O. From 3 moles of manganate, exactly 2 moles of permanganate are produced.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following correctly pairs the intense colors and the magnetic properties of the manganate (MnO4(2-)) and permanganate (MnO4-) ions?
options: MnO4(2-) (Green, Paramagnetic) ; MnO4- (Purple, Diamagnetic)
MnO4(2-) (Green, Diamagnetic) ; MnO4- (Purple, Paramagnetic)
MnO4(2-) (Purple, Paramagnetic) ; MnO4- (Green, Diamagnetic)
Both ions are Paramagnetic and their colors arise strictly from d-d transitions.
questions.explanation: Manganate (Mn^6+, d^1) is green and paramagnetic due to 1 unpaired electron. Permanganate (Mn^7+, d^0) is purple and diamagnetic. The purple color arises from Ligand-to-Metal Charge Transfer (LMCT).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: During the acidic disproportionation of potassium manganate (K2MnO4), what is its effective equivalent weight? (Let M = molar mass of K2MnO4)
questions.explanation: In 3MnO4(2-) -> 2MnO4- + MnO2, 2 moles of electrons are transferred for every 3 moles of reactant used. The n-factor per mole = Total e- transferred / Moles of reactant = 2/3. Equivalent Weight = M / (2/3) = 3M / 2.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Why is the +2 oxidation state of copper vastly more stable than the +1 state in aqueous medium, despite the +1 state having a stable completely filled 3d^10 configuration?
options: Cu^2+ has a much lower effective nuclear charge than Cu^+.
The massive negative hydration enthalpy of the small, highly charged Cu^2+ ion more than compensates for the high second ionization enthalpy required to form it.
Water acts as a strong oxidizing agent, forcing Cu^+ to oxidize into Cu^2+.
Cu^+ has unpaired electrons that make it radically unstable in water.
questions.explanation: In aqueous solutions, thermodynamic stability is heavily driven by hydration enthalpy. The Cu^2+ ion is smaller and more highly charged, yielding a massive exothermic hydration enthalpy that offsets the high energy cost of the second ionization enthalpy.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Transition metals and their compounds behave as excellent catalysts. Which of the following factors is the LEAST responsible for this catalytic activity?
options: Ability to adopt multiple variable oxidation states.
Provision of a large surface area for the adsorption of reactant molecules.
High tendency to form intermediate coordination complexes.
Their highly constant and rigid atomic radii across the series.
questions.explanation: Catalysis is driven by variable oxidation states, complex formation, and surface area. Atomic radii variations (or the lack thereof) play virtually no role in their catalytic mechanisms.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Based on the comparison of ionic radii curves, what is the fundamental quantum-mechanical reason for the Actinoid contraction being greater from element to element than the Lanthanoid contraction?
options: The 5f orbitals have a more diffuse shape and provide significantly poorer shielding of the nuclear charge than the 4f orbitals.
Actinoids possess much higher densities, which mathematically forces the electron cloud to compress faster.
The 6d electrons in Actinoids strongly repel the 5f electrons, pushing them closer to the nucleus.
Lanthanoids form mostly covalent bonds, which artificially inflates their apparent ionic radii.
questions.explanation: Actinoid contraction is greater because the 5f orbitals are larger and more diffuse than 4f orbitals. As a result, 5f electrons shield the increasingly large nuclear charge very poorly, causing a more pronounced element-to-element shrinkage in ionic radii.
questions.imagePrompt: A line graph comparing the ionic radii of M^3+ ions across the Lanthanoid series (La to Lu) and the Actinoid series (Ac to Lr). Both curves slope downwards, but the curve for the Actinoid series exhibits a steeper, more pronounced drop from element to element compared to the Lanthanoid curve.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Identify the INCORRECT statement regarding the comparative chemistry of Actinoids and Lanthanoids.
options: Actinoids exhibit a much larger number of variable oxidation states than Lanthanoids.
Both series display a steady decrease in their atomic and ionic sizes with increasing atomic number.
Actinoids possess a significantly lower tendency to form coordination complexes compared to Lanthanoids.
The 5f, 6d, and 7s orbitals in Actinoids are of comparable energies, which allows for greater electron participation in bonding.
questions.explanation: Actinoids actually have a *higher* tendency to form complexes than Lanthanoids because of their higher nuclear charge density and the spatial extension of the 5f orbitals which participate more readily in bonding.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Consider Group 6 elements: Chromium (Cr), Molybdenum (Mo), and Tungsten (W). Which of the following statements correctly applies the d-block oxidation state stability trend?
options: Cr(VI) is highly stable and inert, while W(VI) in WO4(2-) is a powerful oxidizing agent.
Cr(VI) in dichromate is a strong oxidizing agent because it easily reduces to Cr(III), whereas Mo(VI) and W(VI) compounds are highly stable and do not act as oxidizing agents.
All Group 6 elements are equally stable in their +6 oxidation states due to identical valence electron counts.
Tungsten prefers a +3 oxidation state over +6 because of the immense shielding effect of its 4f electrons.
questions.explanation: In the d-block, higher oxidation states become *more* stable down a group. Therefore, Cr(VI) is unstable (acts as a strong oxidizing agent to become +3), while heavier Mo(VI) and W(VI) are highly stable and generally unreactive.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: What is the primary composition of Mischmetall, an alloy extensively used in lighter flints?
options: ~ 95% Actinoid metal, ~ 5% Copper, and traces of Zinc.
~ 95% Lanthanoid metal, ~ 5% Iron, and traces of S, C, Ca, and Al.
~ 50% Titanium, ~ 50% Iron, and traces of Carbon.
~ 80% Copper, ~ 20% Tin, and traces of Lanthanum.
questions.explanation: Mischmetall is a rare-earth alloy consisting primarily of lanthanoid metals (~95%, mostly Ce and La), iron (~5%), and trace non-metals/metals like S, C, Ca, and Al.
